welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.subtitle: Three quick steps to show how Accanto works. Skip anytime.

step1.title: A circle for who you care for
step1.body: Each person you look after has their own circle: information, documents, and the people helping—all in one place.

step2.title: Shared journal
step2.body: One entry at a time. Symptoms, appointments, decisions—in order, easy to find when it matters.

step3.title: Invite whoever you want
step3.body: Add family or friends to the circle. You decide what each person can see. You can also start on your own.

difficultDay.title: A hard day
difficultDay.intro: When everything weighs on you, try one of these small gestures. They don't fix things, but they let you breathe.
suggestions: Take three slow breaths, doing nothing else.
Drink a glass of water. Eat something, even a little.
Write a single sentence in the journal, even a harsh one. It doesn't have to be nice.
Send a message to someone you trust: just “I'm having a hard day” is enough.
If you can, step outside for five minutes. Even just to the doorstep.
You're not alone. You're doing a lot.
difficultDay.needHelp: If you feel you can't cope, talking to someone helps.
difficultDay.emergency: If there's a medical emergency, call 112.

selfCare.title: Caring for yourself
selfCare.intro: People who care for someone they love often forget to look after themselves. It isn't selfishness — it's necessary maintenance, like the car that carries everyone home.

tips.0: Drink a glass of water, now, before going back to anything else.
tips.1: Three slow breaths: in for 4, out for 6. Just that.
tips.2: For five minutes put your phone on silent and do one thing for yourself.
tips.3: Send a message to someone who loves you: even a plain 'hi' counts.
tips.4: Step outside your door, look around, feel the air.
tips.5: Eat something, even a little. Don't skip meals.
tips.6: Lie down for five minutes. You don't have to sleep, just stop.
tips.7: Write one sentence: what feels heaviest today.
tips.8: Think of one thing you did well today. Just one.
tips.9: Ask yourself: is there one thing I can hand off to someone today?

burnout.title: Signs not to ignore
burnout.intro: Caregiver burnout is real. If you recognise several of these together, don't wait.
signs: Irritability toward the person you care for
Thoughts of running away or not being able to go on
burnout.outro: If more than three of these feel familiar, talk to your doctor or a listening service. It isn't weakness — it's useful information.

rest.title: The rule of rest
rest.body: Rest isn't a reward, it's fuel. Schedule rest the way you schedule medication: at fixed times, even when it 'doesn't feel necessary'. By the time the need hits, it's often too late.

boundaries.title: Healthy limits
boundaries.intro: Saying 'no' to something means saying 'yes' to something else: to you, to your health, to care that lasts.
points: You are not required to be available 24/7.
Asking for help isn't failure: it's strategy.
Sharing tasks with people around you (family, services) is an act of responsibility.
Mixed feelings are normal: love and exhaustion, gratitude and anger. They coexist.

selfCare.disclaimer: These pages do not replace medical or psychological advice. If you are suffering, talk to a professional.
